messages:
Maya: hey — has anyone seen a weird jump in the p99 for /v1/generate after the canary this morning? counts look different vs p50/p95 :thinking:
Sam: can you paste the dashboard link and sample counts? p99 jumps usually mean a small high-latency tail got sampled more
Maya: https://dashboard.internal/redwood/latency?endpoint=/v1/generate
Maya: p50 48ms p95 120ms p99 420ms earlier, now p99 reported ~1.6s but p95 unchanged. sample_count for p99 slice shows 18 -> 4
Alex: hmm, that 18->4 sounds like we're collapsing sampling buckets somewhere. Are these client-side sampled traces making it into the rollup? or did the routing change alter sampling identity? @deploy-bot did the canary change sampling config?
deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-19T08:12:03Z applied: "gateway: route-weighting + route-sampler v2" (rev 8a4c1)
Jordan: quick note — telemetry pipeline applies two filters: gateway route-sampler (client-provided tag preserved) and ingestion-side reservoir-sampler for high-throughput endpoints. If a tag is missing we fallback to ingestion-sampler which uses a different seed, so sample identity can flip.
Priya: are we sure the dashboard percentiles are grouped by sample provenance? I.e. p99 may be calculated over mixing of sample sets with different selection probabilities
Maya: not sure. I ran this query against telemetry-store:

```
SELECT pctile(tdigest, 0.99) as p99, sum(count) as n
FROM latency_rollups
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND window='5m' AND tag='region:us-west'
GROUP BY sample_origin
```

Maya: results: sample_origin=gateway: p99=430ms n=18 ; sample_origin=ingest-reservoir: p99=1.6s n=4
Sam: ok that explains the UI number — the dashboard merges origins by default and shows a single p99 computed from aggregated t-digests. mixing t-digests from different sample populations with different biases can produce odd pctl jumps
Alex: right — when you combine a small heavy-tail sample (n=4) with a larger light-tail (n=18) the merged t-digest percentile can be dominated by the heavy samples depending on compression parameters
Jordan: devex/console idea: show sample_origin as a small pill next to the percentile (gateway | ingest | client) and default to a stacked view rather than naive merge. Also show effective sample_weight or n for each percentile slice :bulb:
Maya: that UI would help. For now, can we make the query on the dashboard prefer the largest-n origin for percentiles unless user selects "merge"? Fallback to merged only if none has n>k
Priya: threshold idea: prefer origin with n >= max_n * 0.25? otherwise show merged + badge "multi-origin". we should avoid hiding legitimate high-tail signals though
Sam: operationally, the root cause here is the canary changed the gateway sampler seed logic so more tail traces escaped the gateway sampler earlier. So ingestion-reservoir picked up a few high-latency requests and they skew the merged p99
Alex: fix options:
- make dashboard merge logic weight-aware (prefer origin with highest effective sample_weight)
- surface per-origin percentiles by default for p95/p99 when sample_origins>1
- change ingestion-reservoir to annotate provenance consistently (so we don't lose gateway tag)

Jordan: low-effort quickwin: add a tooltip on percentile that shows per-origin breakdown and counts. then we can iterate UI patterns.
Maya: agreed. opened ENG-8473 to add a tooltip + per-origin list on hover. tagging @Sam to own the query change + Priya for server-side annotation fix
Sam: I'll follow up with a PR to the dashboard query to prefer single-origin pctl when its n >= 10 and >= 30% of total. I'll add the tooltip link to ENG-8473
Priya: I'll audit the ingestion pipeline to ensure gateway provenance tags survive the reservoir-sampler and push a bugfix if needed
Alex: can we add a short console banner when percentiles are merged across origins: "Percentiles are merged across multiple sampling origins which can distort high-percentile values. Hover for breakdown."? keeps users from panicking
Maya: love it. for now I'll pin this thread to keep folks updated. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam: looping in @Jordan for UX followups once the tooltip exists
Jordan: will prototype the tooltip/pill tomorrow. rough sketch: pill shows origin + n + sample_rate and a small sparklines for that origin. low friction
Maya: perfect. closing the loop: root cause = canary sampler seed change exposed heavy-tail into ingest-reservoir -> merged t-digest skew. short term: tooltip + query prefer large-n origin. long term: provenance hygiene and UI improvements.
Priya: noted. will post pipeline findings here when I have them.
Maya: thanks — keeping an eye on the p99 now :eyes:
